<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/package.json`, `packages/verify/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **5** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f931e765b72fcdc49f6c28d59e0155b10f79b8ee` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `930f2100e098881db7aebc46fa73476cee55edb0` — the merge of head `0c232d83fb586b00a33dab206e4279a1fcaab8b8` into base `f931e765b72fcdc49f6c28d59e0155b10f79b8ee`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

git fetch origin 930f2100e098881db7aebc46fa73476cee55edb0 && git checkout 930f2100e098881db7aebc46fa73476cee55edb0

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0c232d83fb586b00a33dab206e4279a1fcaab8b8`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23088 (its body and all six comments — triage, the claim, both `os-dev-report`s, the seat's ruling and its ACCEPT, the last four read as claims to test); PR #23127 (its body, its 10-file list, the three-dot diff against `origin/main`); and the check-runs on the head, latest run per name: 35 `success`, 7 `skipped` by the roster, no failure. Reference reads on `origin/main`, read-only: `serve.ts`'s `hostConfigMetadataDoor` and its `kernel.use` site, `stackBootPlugins`, `isHostConfig`, the kernel's `use` and `registerPluginByName`, `MetadataPlugin`'s options, repository attach and HMR mount, `FileSystemRepository.start`, the #21876 seam pin, the two artifact-door dogfood proofs. Rules judged against: AGENTS.md Prime Directives #10 and #12, Post-Task Checklist step 3. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The composition against its published rule — right.**
- Option for option: `new MetadataPlugin({ watch: false, config: { bootstrap: 'lazy' }, rootDir: hostRoot })` is what `serve.ts` builds for `hostConfigMetadataDoor`: no `artifactSource`, no `artifactWatch`, `registerSystemObjects` at its default. `rootDir`: `serve` hands `servedAppRootOrCwd()`, the harness `opts.hostRoot ?? process.cwd()` — the same anchor (the app's root, cwd when none is given).
- Slot for slot: `serve` registers its HTTP server, then the door at its own `kernel.use` site with no catch, then the app's `plugins` with the `AppPlugin` wrap appended; the harness registers the door right after `HonoServerPlugin` and before `AppPlugin`, with no catch. Same order, same failure mode: a door that cannot compose fails the boot instead of falling back to the matcher-less occupant quietly — Prime Directive #12's shape, no lenient fallback in a consumer.
- The "already in `plugins`" rule: `serve` tests `p?.name === 'com.objectstack.metadata' || p?.constructor?.name === 'MetadataPlugin'` over `stackBootPlugins(config)`, which returns the RAW `config.plugins` array; the harness tests the same two keys over `opts.extraPlugins` plus the raw `config.plugins`. Equivalent, with the same blind spot on both sides: a string specifier that materializes into a `MetadataPlugin` is not seen, the door composes, and the kernel's last-one-wins supersedes it with one `warn` — the net occupant is still the app's own, which is what the changeset promises. Adding `extraPlugins` to the scan is the right reading of the harness's own precedence rule.
- Composed where `serve` would not: `serve` gates this door on `isHostConfig(config)` (an instantiated plugin in `plugins`) and on no dev artifact door; the harness composes it for every configuration, a library configuration included, where `serve` would boot `createStandaloneStack`'s artifact-backed door (`securityMetadataRegistrar: 'artifact-door'`) instead. Judged right and not this PR's gap: ruling A already mounts the host-configuration path for every configuration (`AppPlugin(config)`, registrar `'app-plugin'`), and the artifact-less door is the one door consistent with that registrar — an artifact door beside an `'app-plugin'` registrar is exactly the hybrid the showcase file used to hand in, a boot no production composition runs. The docblock names the modelled shape ("for a host configuration"). The library-configuration divergence predates this PR (#22301) and is outside it. `BootOptions.artifact` is unaffected: `AppPlugin` loads the artifact, the door reads nothing, as the docblock's "read from `config` either way" says.
- Composed here that `serve` would not for the same configuration: the dev-only HMR route. `MetadataPlugin.start` mounts `/api/v1/dev/metadata-events` only under `NODE_ENV=development`; the harness forces that posture (pre-existing, "mirrors `objectstack dev`"), so the route answers 200 here and would not under a production `serve`. The changeset states it. Right.
- Writes: `FileSystemRepository` attaches at `hostRoot/.objectstack/metadata`; `start()` scans and deliberately does not `mkdir` (#7000, "attaching is not a write"), and `disableWatch` holds because `watch: false`. The dev's "nothing written" census is what the code predicts.
- The exception list stays the two it named (MCP endpoint, pinyin search). No third exception was owed: the measurement moved nothing the suite pins.

**2. What moves for every caller of `bootStack` — right, stated by its answers.**
- Moves on every boot: the `metadata` occupant (a plain fallback object, `__serviceInfo.status` `degraded`, no `matchEndpoint` → `NodeMetadataManager` with one); `kernel.hasPlugin('com.objectstack.metadata')`; a declared `apis` endpoint's answer (404 `ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND` → 401 or its declared answer); `AppPlugin`'s no-matcher warning (gone); `GET /api/v1/discovery` `services.metadata.status` (`degraded` → `available`); `GET /api/v1/dev/metadata-events` (404 → 200); and three boot log lines (`lazy bootstrap`, `FileSystemRepository attached`, `Registered system metadata objects`).
- Does not move, per the census read as a claim and consistent with the code: the 22 `/meta` type bodies, the security registrar (`AppPlugin` once, same counts — the door has no artifact and reads none of the stack), the registry object set, `sys_metadata*` rows (0), boot time.
- A published caller's test CAN break: one that pinned a declared endpoint's 404 under the harness, the fallback's `__serviceInfo` (as this repo's own `external-validate-start-ordering` did, and had to move), the plugin's absence, or the warning line. The changeset states every moved answer — the occupant, the endpoint answers, the precedence rule, discovery, the HMR route, `/meta` unchanged — so a reader who greps `degraded` or `404` lands on the sentence; it states them as answers, not as "a test that pinned the old fallback now fails". Adequate for a patch to a harness whose consumers are test suites. Noted, not a failing finding.

**3. `packages/verify/package.json` gains `@objectstack/metadata` — right.** `harness.ts` imports it at module top and ships it in `dist/`, so `dependencies`, beside every other runtime plugin the harness mounts, is the right section — not `devDependencies`, not a peer. No cycle: `@objectstack/metadata` depends on `core`, `metadata-core`, `metadata-fs`, `spec` and `types`, none of which depends on `verify`; `Validate Package Dependencies` is green on the head. `pnpm-lock.yaml` moves the one importer link and nothing else (+3). The `vitest.config.ts` alias is the anchored form the `core` entry uses and the remedy `check:test-source-alias` prescribes (`Lint & Repo Gates` green, red on this at round 0). The file's header still explains only the `core` entry — a comment nit, not a defect.

**4. The flipped dogfood precondition — right, and it bears weight.** The case pins the occupant by public reads: `hasPlugin('com.objectstack.metadata')`, `toBeInstanceOf(MetadataManager)` (`NodeMetadataManager extends MetadataManager`, so the check holds on the real occupant), and `matchEndpoint` a function. The dev's ablation leg 3 — door removed, `verify` rebuilt, the marker preflight-absent from all six built files — reds it at `hasPlugin` with both federation cases green: the pin's weight and its independence from the federation answers, both shown. The #21876 ordering fix stays pinned at its seam: `external-validate-reads-live-registry.test.ts`'s case "asks for the registry when validation runs, so an engine registered after init is read". What is no longer guarded: the dogfood-level, HTTP-door reproduction of a matcher-less composition (the fallback registered after every `init()`); that composition now exists only on `OS_MODE=off` boots and embedders, and its mechanism is held by the seam pin. Ruling A is the right one of the three: B (a stand-in named `com.objectstack.metadata` that registers nothing) declares a plugin the runtime does not deliver, Prime Directive #10's corollary; C drops the HTTP federation proof no other layer holds.

**5. The showcase file's hand-added plugin removed — right.** The artifact door's `apis:` → `api` ingestion keeps two proofs that hand an artifact-backed `MetadataPlugin` through `extraPlugins` with `artifactSource: { mode: 'local-file' }` (`declarative-endpoint-policy`, `declarative-endpoint-anonymous-guest`); under the precedence rule the composed door is skipped there, so both still measure the artifact door, and `multi-package-artifact`'s second block does the same. The showcase file still writes the build-shaped artifact and its section 0 reads it back, so the E7 publish-gate proof keeps its subject. Its new `rootDir` is the showcase directory (the file `chdir`s there); attach writes nothing. The header sentences match what the boot now does.

**6. Every docs sentence against the diff — true.** The `bootStack` docblock: the composition sentence names the plugin and the precedence rule, the exception list is unchanged. The changeset: the options, `rootDir` = `BootOptions.hostRoot` (cwd when unset, as that option documents), "reads none of the stack", the precedence rule, the three moved answers, `/meta` unchanged. The three test headers and the `multi-package-artifact` comment. The `start-ordering` header's "`serve` and `start` give a host configuration" matches `serve.ts`'s own note that `os start`'s serve child takes the door's branch. One stale sentence stays in the tree outside the claimed surface: `packages/services/service-datasource/src/plugin.ts` about `:83`, "`objectstack start` composes no metadata plugin", false since PR #23078 — a code comment with no reader harmed, noted by the seat; not a filing class under Prime Directive #10. The runtime's own `datasource-*.test.ts` comments ("host-config shape: NO MetadataPlugin") describe kernels those files build themselves, not `bootStack`, and stay true.

**7. The verify pin, `harness.metadata-door.test.ts` — right.** The composite case was ablated red (leg 1: matcher `undefined`, 404 and 404, one matcher warning). The second case's "never registered" claim rests on its supersede filter, which bears weight: `registerPluginByName` warns with a structured `plugin: name` field on a duplicate name, and the door registers before `extraPlugins`, so a composed-then-superseded door is caught by exactly that field. Nit: the first case's warning filter includes `line.includes('MetadataPlugin')`, a prose match, while the header says "never by prose"; the composite's other three fields carry the weight.

**8. CI on the head.** `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (not governed), `Validate Package Dependencies`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, all six `Test Core` shards, the four type checks: green. The dogfood shards skip on a PR by design (#22998, the `Dogfood Regression Gate` context counts zero attestations), so the whole-suite result on this head is the dev's local run — 258 passed, 1 skipped, 1 red, judged in ③ — and the full battery measures it after landing.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/verify` `patch` — matches. The diff makes a published package keep its own published rule (the docblock ships in its `.d.ts`): a fix in a released package, `patch` by Post-Task Checklist step 3, never none. `Clause-②: no` holds: `packages/verify/src/index.ts` is untouched, `BootOptions` and `VerifyStack` are unchanged, no authorable key moves, no accept set widens or narrows (a configuration that booted still boots, measured over the whole dogfood suite; a `MetadataPlugin` in `plugins` or `extraPlugins` is honoured as before). The new runtime dependency is additive. The changeset carries the `Clause-②` line; no breaking marker and no migration are owed. `Check Changeset` green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Round 0 `blocked_on` and deviation 1 (two edits outside the surface): extended by the seat's ruling, done in round 1 one commit per item; the `start-ordering` diff has no line inside either federation case. Answered.
- Round 0 deviation 2 (a stray `/build-base.pid` at the dev container's filesystem root): outside the repository, nothing lands; an operator cleanup note. Answered.
- **Round 0 deviation 3 — ESCALATED to the maintainer.** The dev printed the value of `OS_FLEET_PRIVATE_KEY` into round 0's local tool output and asks that the key be treated as exposed to that transcript. Neither the seat's ruling nor its ACCEPT addresses it. It is not a diff defect and not repository state, so it does not move this verdict; it is a credential-handling incident for the maintainer's rotation decision. No value is reproduced here.
- Round 0 deviations 4 to 9 (the first ablation attempt a non-run, replaced by the second; trailer form per AGENTS.md; scratch instruments uncommitted; the gitignored `showcase_external.db` cleaned; `Fixes` on line 1 while the card is not in a decision box, the `Part-of` check green; zero label writes): answered.
- Round 0 `open_questions`: ruled A; judged right (① 4).
- Round 0 `out_of_scope_findings`: the stale `service-datasource` comment (① 6); the 17 `chdir` files' leftover database (pre-existing test-infrastructure state, outside this surface); the two comment sentences (fixed in round 1). Noted-not-filed is the right class for the first two.
- Round 1 `deviations`: the worktree recreated at the branch tip; a lock queue timeout re-queued; a stale gate runner stopped by pid; the `describe` title moved with the header; the precondition by public reads; `@objectstack/cli` `verify-*` not re-run locally this round — `Test Core` on the head covers that package's unit tier, green; no environment value printed this round; database cleanup. Answered.
- Round 1 `out_of_scope_findings` — the one red dogfood file, `mail-message-pool-read-gate.dogfood.test.ts`. Judged `main`'s own red, not this PR's: (a) the dev's CONTROL ran both legs inside the lock — door as built, and door removed with `verify` rebuilt and the marker preflight-absent — and both red at the same `beforeAll` assertion (fixture permission set seeded: expected undefined to be truthy), 9 skipped; (b) #23148, the hourly full-run card on `main`, names the same file, line and assertion on `main`'s own run of `287fd6e5d0`, with PR #22900 ("no seeder or materializer writes a `sys_permission_set` row") in the range since the last green run; (c) the mechanism matches — the fixture reads a `sys_permission_set` row that #22900 stopped writing, and this PR's door registers nothing of the stack (security registrar and `/meta/permission` bodies unchanged in the census); (d) the fix is dispatched on #23056 in another lane. Nothing is skipped or narrowed here. The ACCEPT's sequencing behind #23148 is the two-speed doctrine's, not this record's.
- Prime Directive #10: no defect, contract violation or authoring trap found in this diff goes unfiled; the one defect found beside it (the `main` red) has its card and its fix in flight.
